content: 1. Sulfamethoxazole metabolism is influenced by hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown or minor. 2. Fexinidazole increases trimethoprim levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used due to the risk of adverse effects associated with CYP3A4 substrates. Fexinidazole is a CYP3A4 inhibitor, and close monitoring is recommended. 3. Trimethoprim and finerenone both elevate serum potassium levels. Therapy should be modified, and serum potassium levels should be closely monitored. Finerenone dosage adjustments should be based on current serum potassium concentrations, as outlined in prescribing information. 4. Sulfamethoxazole and flecainide both prolong the QTc interval. Similarly, flecainide and trimethoprim also increase the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 5. Fluconazole and trimethoprim both increase the QTc interval, as do sulfamethoxazole and fluconazole. Fluconazole also increases sulfamethoxazole levels or effects by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown or minor. Close monitoring is recommended. 6. Fluoxetine and trimethoprim both prolong the QTc interval. Fluoxetine also increases sulfamethoxazole levels or effects by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 7. Fluphenazine and trimethoprim both increase the QTc interval, as do fluphenazine and sulfamethoxazole. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 8. Sulfamethoxazole increases flurbiprofen levels or effects by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown or minor. 9. Sulfamethoxazole increases fluvastatin levels or effects by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown or minor. 10. Fluvoxamine and trimethoprim both prolong the QTc interval, as do fluvoxamine and sulfamethoxazole. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 11. Sulfamethoxazole reduces folic acid levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown or minor. 12. Sulfamethoxazole increases the effects of fondaparinux by reducing its metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. 13. Sulfamethoxazole and formoterol both prolong the QTc interval, as do formoterol and trimethoprim. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 14. Sulfamethoxazole and foscarnet both increase the QTc interval, as do foscarnet and trimethoprim. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 15. Trimethoprim and fosinopril both elevate serum potassium levels. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Trimethoprim reduces urinary potassium excretion, which may lead to hyperkalemia, particularly at high doses, in renal insufficiency, or when combined with other hyperkalemia-inducing drugs. 16. Sulfamethoxazole increases fosphenytoin levels by reducing its metabolism. Fosphenytoin decreases trimethoprim levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown or minor. 17. Furosemide increases sulfamethoxazole levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown or minor. 18. Ganciclovir increases sulfamethoxazole toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown or minor. 19. Sulfamethoxazole increases glimepiride levels through plasma protein binding competition. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 20. Sulfamethoxazole increases glipizide levels through plasma protein binding competition. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 21. Glucarpidase reduces sulfamethoxazole levels by increasing its metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Glucarpidase also reduces trimethoprim levels by increasing its metabolism. 22. Sulfamethoxazole increases glyburide levels through plasma protein binding competition and by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 23. Haloperidol and trimethoprim both prolong the QTc interval, as do sulfamethoxazole and haloperidol. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 24. Sulfamethoxazole increases the effects of heparin by reducing its metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. 25. Hydrochlorothiazide increases trimethoprim levels through competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown or minor. 26. Sulfamethoxazole increases ibuprofen levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown or minor. 27. Ibutilide and trimethoprim both prolong the QTc interval, as do sulfamethoxazole and ibutilide. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. 28. Idelalisib increases trimethoprim levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. 29. Sulfamethoxazole and iloperidone both prolong the QTc interval, as do iloperidone and trimethoprim. Iloperidone increases trimethoprim levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 30. Imatinib increases sulfamethoxazole levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 31. Sulfamethoxazole and imidapril increase the risk of hyperkalemia through pharmacodynamic synergy. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 32. Imipramine and sulfamethoxazole both prolong the QTc interval, as do imipramine and trimethoprim. Sulfamethoxazole reduces imipramine levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown or minor. 33. Sulfamethoxazole and indapamide both prolong the QTc interval, as do indapamide and trimethoprim. Indapamide increases sulfamethoxazole levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown or minor. 34. Indinavir increases trimethoprim levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 35. Indomethacin increases sulfamethoxazole levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown or minor. 36. Trimethoprim and irbesartan both elevate serum potassium levels. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Trimethoprim reduces urinary potassium excretion, which may lead to hyperkalemia. 37. Isavuconazonium sulfate increases trimethoprim levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown or minor. 38. Sulfamethoxazole decreases folic acid levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown or minor. 39. Sulfamethoxazole increases lacosamide levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 40. Trimethoprim increases lamivudine effects by competing for renal tubular clearance. Sulfamethoxazole increases lamivudine levels by reducing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown or minor. 41. Sulfamethoxazole and lapatinib both prolong the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 42. Larotrectinib increases trimethoprim levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown or minor. 43. Leflunomide increases sulfamethoxazole levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown or minor. 44. Lenacapavir increases trimethoprim levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 45. Sulfamethoxazole increases lesinurad levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 46. Leucovorin reduces trimethoprim effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. 47. Sulfamethoxazole and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval, as do levofloxacin and trimethoprim. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 48. Levoketoconazole and trimethoprim both prolong the QTc interval, as do sulfamethoxazole and levoketoconazole. Levoketoconazole increases sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism, respectively. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown or minor. 49. Levoleucovorin reduces trimethoprim effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. 50. Trimethoprim reduces the effects of oral contraceptives containing levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 51. Linezolid increases sulfamethoxazole levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown or minor. 52. Trimethoprim and lisinopril both elevate serum potassium levels. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Trimethoprim reduces urinary potassium excretion, which may lead to hyperkalemia. 53. Lofepramine and sulfamethoxazole both prolong the QTc interval, as do lofepramine and trimethoprim. Sulfamethoxazole reduces lofepramine levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown or minor. 54. Lonafarnib increases trimethoprim levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used.
